Pervasive

per-VAY-siv -- stress on the second syllable, VAY. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pervasive is spreading widely through an area.

A pervasive smell of woodsmoke hung in every room of the cabin, from the attic to the cellar.

Worked Example

After one week, the new pop song plays in the grocery store, leaks from passing car windows, hums under television ads, and loops in everyone's heads at bedtime.

The song has become pervasive -- it has spread through every corner of daily life until there is nowhere it cannot be heard. Pervasive describes what spreads widely through every part of an area, a group, or a culture.

How Pervasive Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

widespread

widespread: found over a large area

ubiquitous

ubiquitous: seeming to be everywhere at once

omnipresent

omnipresent: present in all places at all times

Antonyms

confined

confined: kept within limits

localized

localized: restricted to one small area

How Strong Is It? — widespread → pervasive → omnipresent

widespread vs. pervasive

widespread vs. pervasive: Widespread is flatter and weaker than pervasive -- a widespread custom is found in many places, while a pervasive one has soaked into every layer of life, felt even where it is not seen.

omnipresent vs. pervasive

omnipresent vs. pervasive: Omnipresent goes past pervasive: a pervasive influence spreads through nearly everything, while an omnipresent one is literally everywhere at once, impossible to escape for even a moment.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — per-

Prefix — per-: through (Latin)

Root — vas

Root — vas: to go, to walk (from Latin vadere — the same root spelled vad in invade)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: having the quality of (Latin -ivus)

Put it together

Put it together: Per- ('through') + vas ('to go, to walk' — from Latin vadere) + -ive ('having the quality of'): 'going through.' Something pervasive does exactly that — it walks through the whole of a place or culture, passing into every room, every layer, every corner.

Use the root in a new word: invade

Use the root in a new word: invade: Ants invaded the picnic basket the moment we turned our backs.

Root Check

Word Choice

Pervasive pairs with things that spread through other things: a pervasive odor, pervasive anxiety, the pervasive influence of advertising. It leans negative -- moods, problems, and smells are pervasive more often than joys are -- and it stresses reaching into every part, not just covering a wide area.
